title: Proof, pending review
subtitle: A claimed ETH refutation under review, Anthropic's S-1 numbers, a disputed breach, a Lean-proved backend, a Triassic sea amphibian
editor_note: Today is full of claims that are not yet facts. OpenAI says its models helped make three discoveries, the boldest a claimed refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis; Ryan Williams, Russell Impagliazzo and Mohan Paturi are organizing an open review, and until it ends the right word is "claimed". Anthropic's S-1 is the opposite kind of document: numbers filed under disclosure rules. The Cathedral breach story sits in between, a reported claim the company disputes. Your saves fit the theme: Nyxis proves authorization safety in Lean, but only inside the assumptions it writes down, and Huntley pipes little bots together. Field notes add agents that never rethink a strategy and a KV-cache leak at Cloudflare. Japan has Rakuten Travel's breach and Rapidus hiring help in India. Further out: gas-powered data centers, India's press against a privacy law, a phonetic map, a marine amphibian, Troy's first flute, and a Tao puzzle to end on.

sections.headline: OpenAI claims AI-assisted discoveries in mathematics, computer science and physics
sections.deck: Harmonic analysis, complexity theory and quantum field theory, announced together. The biggest, a claimed refutation of ETH, now goes to an independent review.
sections.art_alt: Three glowing orbits crossing around a bright core on deep purple
sections.why: If even one holds, AI moves from helping with proofs to producing results experts must check. Read it as a claim for now.

sections.headline: Anthropic's S-1, cheaper Terra, a disputed breach, Microsoft buyouts

items.headline: Anthropic's S-1: $16.3B H1 revenue and ~$265.6B in compute it must pay for
items.note: Net loss $80.7B, mostly a non-cash note charge. Founders keep 50.1% of the vote; ticker ANT on Nasdaq.
items.why: The first audited look at a frontier lab's economics: the compute bill is owed whether or not usage shows up.

items.headline: GPT-6.1 Terra: better than 5.6 Terra at half the API price
items.note: Pitched for computer use. OpenAI still points complex coding to Sol or Astra.
items.why: A cheaper default for agent loops; worth re-running your evals and costs on it.

items.headline: WaPo: ex-DOGE researchers' agents reached Anthropic's Slack in under 12 hours
items.note: Reportedly via third-party vendor software under the bug bounty. Anthropic disputes the scope; no write-up yet.
items.why: Agents finding the weak vendor link fast is plausible, but the details are one side's account so far.

items.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 staff
items.note: Gergely Orosz: hard news from a stable employer, but more humane than waiting for layoffs.
items.why: A signal of how Big Tech is reshaping headcount as AI spending climbs.

sections.deck: A big claim, and how experts are holding it.

sections.headline: A claimed refutation of ETH, and an open review to test it
sections.deck: OpenAI's paper says 3SAT runs in about exp(n/(log n)^{1/2+o(1)}) time. Williams, Impagliazzo and Paturi will organize an independent examination.
sections.art_alt: A lattice of purple nodes with one dashed path traced across it to a circled end point
sections.why: ETH underpins many lower bounds. A refutation would be historic, so the review matters more than the headline.

sections.quote: An internal model at OpenAI has produced a claimed refutation of ETH!

sections.headline: Take it seriously, or step away from AI?
sections.verdict: Both are reactions before the facts are in. Gowers treats the claim as momentous if true; the pledge refuses AI math on principle. The open review will say whether the proof holds, and that is the part worth waiting for.

items.label: Timothy Gowers
items.note: ETH is the hypothesis that 3SAT needs exponential time; it being false would be very surprising and consequential.
items.why: A Fields medallist engaging with the claim on its merits.

items.label: A pledge against AI math
items.note: Reported: 1,000+ mathematicians commit not to publish AI-generated papers or work with labs; 654 refuse AI entirely.
items.why: Shows how split the field is just as AI results arrive.

sections.deck: What you saved since the last issue.

sections.headline: A backend with a proof attached, and bots in pipelines

items.headline: Nyxis: a Lean-proved guarantee that no request exceeds its permissions
items.note: You maintain the policy; agents can write the rest. Outside the proof: the runtime, a wrong policy, and any second path to the database.
items.why: Today's theme in your own saves: a real proof, valid only inside its written assumptions.

items.headline: Huntley: lots of little bots, piped together like Unix
items.note: His trip bot hands off to an events bot, which trims the list when his flight date arrives.
items.why: Small composable bots are easier to test and swap than one giant agent.

sections.deck: Agents that don't rethink, caches that leak.

sections.headline: Locked-in strategies, and a KV cache shared across requests

items.headline: Coding agents run post-training well but almost never switch strategy
items.note: Only 2.1% of experiment pairs change approach. One human sentence mid-run beat autonomy: GSM8K +17.44pp.
items.why: A cheap habit: at the halfway mark, ask your agent whether the plan itself is right.

items.headline: Cloudflare: a GLM 5.3 config mismatch exposed KV cache pages across requests
items.note: An SGLang bug in disaggregated serving. LMSYS published fixes and steps for operators.
items.why: Inference servers are a new place for data to leak between users. Patch SGLang if you self-host.

items.why: 利用者なら明細の確認を。大手でも漏洩の波は続いている。

items.note: HCLがカルナタカ州に2拠点。2ナノ量産に向けた人材不足を補う。

sections.deck: One step out: power, memory and burgers.

sections.headline: Gas-fired data centers, a memory crunch into 2027, McDonald's as an MCP server

items.headline: Off-grid gas at data centers: 60–80% higher emissions than the grid
items.note: Zeke Hausfather warns it risks locking in fossil dependence.
items.why: The AI build-out's climate cost depends on where the power comes from.

items.headline: Michael Dell: the memory shortage gets worse in 2027
items.note: New fabs take about four years; relief maybe by 2029. Agents changed demand.
items.why: Explains RAM and SSD prices, and why hardware plans may slip.

items.headline: 麦当劳中国把点餐和优惠券做成了 MCP 接口
items.note: 开发者做了省钱技能：说一句“只有二十块”，智能体自己凑券。
items.why: A consumer brand treating agents as customers, ahead of most of the West.

sections.deck: Worth knowing, whatever you work on.

sections.headline: A press fight in India, a phonetic map, a sea amphibian, Troy's first flute

items.headline: India's biggest publishers take Modi's privacy law to the Supreme Court
items.note: Consent and erasure rules, they argue, would let subjects of investigations kill stories and expose sources.
items.why: Privacy law and press freedom can collide; this is the largest test of it in the world's biggest democracy.

items.headline: A 1980s Yugoslav map spells British towns as they sound
items.note: Seen at the Museum of the 80s in Sarajevo.
items.why: Maps show how one place looks from another language.

items.headline: A 237-million-year-old armored amphibian may have lived entirely at sea
items.note: No living amphibian is marine. Steve Brusatte calls it a potential evolutionary gamechanger.
items.why: A rule of biology that looked fixed may have had a Triassic exception.

items.headline: Troy yields its first musical instrument: a 2,800-year-old bone flute
items.note: Plus the head of an Early Bronze Age idol.
items.why: A sound from Homer's city, after 150 years of digging.

sections.headline: Under the lamp
sections.art_alt: A fan of paper cards on a dark desk under a warm desk lamp, the last card gold
sections.caption: A proof is a stack of pages someone has to check, one by one, under a lamp. Today many claims arrived; the checking is the part that lasts.

sections.headline: Terence Tao's Guardian puzzle hides quadratics in a game of plants and coins
sections.note: Set to mark his first general-audience book, Six Math Essentials.
sections.why: After a day of AI math claims, a human mathematician making math playful.
